output.explanation: If report_date is empty, the row passes. If report_date is filled in, the row passes only when visit_date is also filled in and report_date is no more than 10 days (240 hours) after visit_date.
fails_when: report_date is present but visit_date is null. A missing visit_date fails the row.
report_date is more than 10 days (over 240 hours) after visit_date.

Surprising: the expression builds each timestamp by appending the text "T00:00:00Z" to the date with +. This only works if the date columns are handled as ISO date strings. If NAIVE_DATE values are real date types, the + may cause an evaluation error or a type mismatch instead of a clean pass or fail. Check this before relying on the rule.
passes_when: report_date is null, whatever visit_date is.
report_date and visit_date are both present and report_date is 0 to 10 days after visit_date. Exactly 10 days passes, because the bound is inclusive.
report_date is earlier than visit_date. The difference is negative, so it is still within the limit, and nothing flags the odd ordering.
